text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.8% today, continuing a sharp two-week decline of 11.6%. The drop tracks alongside a broader weakening in oil prices: US crude is trading at $99.64 a barrel, down from the $146+ range just two weeks ago. When oil prices fall, exploration and production companies like ConocoPhillips see their profit potential shrink, since the commodity they extract becomes worth less.

The company reported quarterly earnings on November 5th, which may have disappointed investors relative to expectations built on higher oil prices earlier in the month. Beyond that immediate trigger, geopolitical tensions that typically support oil prices—like stalled Iran negotiations—haven't been enough to arrest the broader slide in crude markets, suggesting that supply and demand fundamentals are currently weighing more heavily on the sector than geopolitical risk premiums.
